title: Bit to Byte
prompt: Transform BIT into BOT, then DOT.
hints: Change the vowel first.
BIT -> BOT -> DOT.
explanation: BIT -> BOT (change I to O) -> DOT (change B to D).

title: Hardware Basics
prompt: Group the 4 terms that belong to Computer Hardware.
hints: Look for physical physical computing components.
Silicon chips and storage drives.
explanation: CPU, RAM, GPU, and SSD are physical computer hardware components.

title: Bug to Fix
prompt: Transform BUG into BAG, then BIG, then FIX.
hints: Change U to A first.
BUG -> BAG -> BIG.
explanation: BUG -> BAG -> BIG.

title: Input Devices
prompt: Select the 4 devices used for human computer input.
hints: Devices that send data INTO the computer.
Things you type or click with.
explanation: Mouse, Keyboard, Scanner, and Microphone feed user inputs to a computer.

title: Web to Net
prompt: Shift from WEB to NET in two rungs.
hints: Think of moisture for the middle step.
WEB -> WET -> NET.
explanation: WEB -> WET -> NET.

title: Operating Systems
prompt: Identify the 4 major Operating Systems.
hints: System software that manages computer hardware.
Open source penguins and phone platforms.
explanation: Linux, Windows, macOS, and Android are primary operating systems.

title: App to Apt
prompt: Transform APP to OPT in two rungs.
hints: Apt means suitable or quick to learn.
APP -> APT -> OPT.
explanation: APP -> APT -> OPT.

title: Programming Languages
prompt: Select the 4 coding languages from the list.
hints: Languages used to write application logic.
Snakes, coffee, and oxidized iron.
explanation: Python, Java, Rust, and Kotlin are general purpose programming languages.

title: Run to Fun
prompt: Transform RUN into FUN in two rungs.
hints: Think of the star in our solar system.
RUN -> SUN -> FUN.
explanation: RUN -> SUN -> FUN.

title: Web Frontend Trio
prompt: Select the core frontend web technologies.
hints: The standards powering modern browser execution.
Structure, styling, scripting, and binary modules.
explanation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebAssembly run natively inside web browsers.

title: Code to Mode
prompt: Transform CODE into MODE in two rungs.
hints: Think of a graph or linked list vertex.
CODE -> NODE -> MODE.
explanation: CODE -> NODE (C to N) -> MODE (N to M).

title: Network Protocols
prompt: Select the 4 communication network protocols.
hints: Protocols used on the Internet to transfer files, resolve names, and secure shell.
Hypertext, secure shell, domain names, file transfer.
explanation: HTTP, SSH, DNS, and FTP govern network communication layers.

title: Byte to Gate
prompt: Transform BYTE to GATE in three rungs.
hints: First change Y to I, then B to L.
BYTE -> BITE -> LATE -> GATE.
explanation: BYTE -> BITE -> LATE -> GATE.

title: Linear Data Structures
prompt: Identify the 4 linear data structures.
hints: Elements arranged sequentially.
Push, pop, enqueue, dequeue, indices.
explanation: Array, LinkedList, Stack, and Queue arrange elements in sequential order.

title: Data to Date
prompt: Transform DATA into RATE in two rungs.
hints: Change the last A to E first.
DATA -> DATE -> RATE.
explanation: DATA -> DATE -> RATE.

title: Database Management
prompt: Select the 4 database management systems.
hints: Systems used to store and query persistent data.
Relational elephants, document stores, in-memory caches.
explanation: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and SQLite are database systems.

title: Disk to Risk
prompt: Transform DISK into RISK in one rung.
hints: Only one letter needs to change.
Change D to R.
explanation: DISK -> RISK (replace D with R).

title: Git Version Control
prompt: Select the 4 standard Git commands.
hints: Commands used to save revisions, switch branches, and join trees.
Recording commits and branching operations.
explanation: Commit, Checkout, Rebase, and Merge are foundational Git commands.

title: Loop to Tool
prompt: Transform LOOP into TOLL in three rungs.
hints: Rearrange or transform letters: LOOP -> POOL -> TOOL -> TOLL.
Swimming place then carpenter instrument.
explanation: LOOP -> POOL -> TOOL -> TOLL.

title: Cloud Providers
prompt: Select the 4 major cloud hyperscalers / platforms.
hints: Infrastructure providers hosting modern cloud applications.
Amazon, Microsoft, Google, edge CDN.
explanation: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Cloudflare are prominent cloud computing providers.

title: Stack to Track
prompt: Transform STACK into TRACK in three rungs.
hints: Think of plants (stalk), then cold barrenness (stark).
STACK -> STALK -> STARK -> TRACK.
explanation: STACK -> STALK -> STARK -> TRACK.

title: Cryptographic Primitives
prompt: Select the 4 cryptographic algorithms or hash functions.
hints: Symmetric encryption, asymmetric keys, elliptic curves, cryptographic hashes.
Rijndael, Rivest-Shamir-Adleman, secure hash algorithm.
explanation: AES-256, RSA, SHA-256, and ECDSA are cryptographic algorithms.

title: Parse to Purse
prompt: Transform PARSE into PURSE in one rung.
hints: Change the vowel A.
Change A to U.
explanation: PARSE -> PURSE (change A to U).

title: Sorting Algorithms
prompt: Select the 4 comparison sorting algorithms.
hints: Algorithms that sort items with O(n log n) average complexity.
Divide and conquer, binary heaps, hybrid Python sorter.
explanation: Quicksort, Mergesort, Heapsort, and Timsort are standard sorting algorithms.

title: Graph to Crash
prompt: Transform GRAPH into CRASH in four rungs.
hints: First seize with hands (grasp), then crash.
GRAPH -> GRASP -> CRASH.
explanation: GRAPH -> GRASP -> CRASH.

title: Design Patterns (Gang of Four)
prompt: Select the 4 classic software design patterns.
hints: Creational, behavioral, and structural architectural patterns.
One instance, publish-subscribe, object instantiation.
explanation: Singleton, Observer, Factory, and Decorator are canonical GoF design patterns.

title: Fiber to Cyber
prompt: Transform FIBER into CYBER in three rungs.
hints: Change the first two letters sequentially.
FIBER -> CABER -> CYBER.
explanation: FIBER -> CABER -> CYBER.

title: Compiler Pipeline Stages
prompt: Select the 4 sequential stages of a compiler pipeline.
hints: From source tokens to AST to target machine code.
Tokenization, grammar trees, type checks, emitting binary.
explanation: Lexing, Parsing, Semantic Analysis, and Code Generation form the compiler pipeline.

title: Cache to Catch
prompt: Transform CACHE into CATCH in two rungs.
hints: Substitute the middle letters.
CACHE -> CATCH.
explanation: CACHE -> CATCH.

title: Cybersecurity Attack Vectors
prompt: Select the 4 common cyberattack vectors.
hints: Exploitations compromising application data, memory, or user credentials.
Malicious queries, injected scripts, memory corruption, social engineering.
explanation: SQLi, XSS, Buffer Overflow, and Phishing are major cybersecurity threats.
